Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: single pixel-art character concept roster sheet for Critz Tower Defense.
Create one polished square concept sheet containing EXACTLY 25 distinct small wild animal Workers in an evenly spaced 5 by 5 grid, exactly one full-body character per cell. Title at top verbatim: "CRITZ TOWER DEFENSE". Small subtitle: "25 CRITTER WORKERS". Each cell has its exact species label below. No repeated species. All species naturally no larger than a honey badger; no large animals. These are friendly capable anthropomorphic critter Workers, standing bipedally in 3/4 side-view, oversized expressive animal heads, short rounded bodies, tiny planted feet, species-correct ears/snouts/tails/scales/quills. Preserve animal anatomy and recognizable silhouettes. Tiny mint overalls or aprons with gold button fasteners, some broad cream work hats with mint band adapted around ears, some bare heads to reveal unique species features. Small simple timber-handled work tools or resource bundles in paws for variety, no weapons. Warm handmade Buttonwood style, Terraria level pixel craft but original designs, not copied assets.
Row 1 left to right: 01 Wood Mouse (round ears, thin long tail, tan fur); 02 Sand Lizard (green scales, tapering tail); 03 Fire Salamander (dark plum body, gold spots, moist rounded head); 04 African Brush-tailed Porcupine (compact brown body, short cream quills, bristly tail; small porcupine species); 05 Box Turtle (domed patterned shell, warm green limbs).
Row 2: 06 European Mole (plum-gray fur, pink snout, broad digging paws, tiny eyes); 07 Hedgehog (rounded cream-tipped spine mantle, pointed muzzle); 08 Chipmunk (striped face and back, small upright tail); 09 Red Squirrel (russet fur, magnificent curled fluffy tail, tuft ears); 10 Field Vole (stubby round brown body, tiny ears, short tail).
Row 3: 11 Harvest Shrew (pointed long nose, very tiny charcoal body); 12 Least Weasel (long slender cinnamon body, cream throat, short rounded ears); 13 Stoat (cream belly, black-tipped tail, slightly larger elegant silhouette than weasel); 14 Striped Skunk (black-plum fur, bold cream stripe, raised bushy tail); 15 Pygmy Spotted Skunk (small plum body, distinct cream spots and broken short stripes, separate from striped skunk).
Row 4: 16 Cottontail Rabbit (long ears, cream cotton tail); 17 Pika (round ears, no visible tail, compact buff fur); 18 Jerboa (oversized hind feet, huge ears, long tufted tail); 19 Dormouse (round ears, golden coat, fluffy thin tail); 20 Lesser Tenrec (pointed snout, narrow scruffy spine crest, differs from round hedgehog).
Row 5: 21 Tree Frog (mint-green skin, big gold eyes, round sticky toe pads); 22 Natterjack Toad (stocky olive body, gold dorsal stripe, deliberate chunky skin clusters); 23 Crested Newt (dark body, coral belly, jagged crest, flattened tail, distinct from spotted salamander); 24 Leopard Gecko (gold/cream spotted skin, fat segmented tail, big eyes); 25 Brown Anole (small brown scales, slender tail, subtle coral throat fan; distinct from green sand lizard).
Style: visibly crisp low-resolution pixel art, deliberate large square pixel clusters, consistent pixel size for every character, roughly 32 pixel tall character design enlarged by integer nearest-neighbor for inspection, no antialiasing, no smooth illustration, no blurry painted shading. Concept sheet only, not production sprites. Colored plum/brown contours rather than black, connected base/shadow/highlight clusters, readable silhouettes, quiet negative space. Flat warm cream background, subtle orderly cell spacing, no scenery, no frames obscuring tails, no decorative extra animals. Pixel-style legible dark plum labels.
